title: Evidences that show chemical reaction has occurred
competency: Describe evidences that show a chemical reaction has occurred.

keywords.def: An insoluble solid formed when two solutions react.

en.text: Four signs show a chemical reaction: a colour change, a gas given off (bubbles), a temperature change, and a precipitate (a solid forming). Black copper oxide with sulfuric acid gives a blue solution. Magnesium in acid gives hydrogen bubbles.

screens.title: Fizz!
screens.ask: You add lemon juice to baking soda and it fizzes. What does the fizzing show?
screens.after:
Bubbles mean a gas is given off. Here it is carbon dioxide.
No heat was added, so the water is not boiling.
A new gas is a sign of a chemical reaction.

screens.title: 3.3.2 Evidences
paras: In a chemical reaction, new products form.
A few signs show that a reaction has happened.

screens.title: 1. Colour changes
paras: Gently heat black copper oxide with sulfuric acid.
A blue solution of copper sulfate forms.
Copper oxide (black) + sulfuric acid → copper sulfate (blue) + water

screens.title: 2. A gas is given off
paras: Bubbles of hydrogen gas are given off.
Magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen

screens.title: 3. Temperature change
paras: Heat may be taken in or given out.
Potassium in water gives off hydrogen. So much heat forms that the gas burns.

screens.title: 4. A precipitate forms
paras: Mix silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions.
An insoluble white solid forms. It is called a precipitate: silver chloride.
Silver nitrate + sodium chloride → silver chloride + sodium nitrate

screens.title: Four signs of a chemical reaction
screens.ask: Tap each sign to see the book's example.
items: Black copper oxide and sulfuric acid give a blue copper sulfate solution.
Magnesium in hydrochloric acid gives bubbles of hydrogen gas.
Potassium in water gives so much heat that the hydrogen burns.
Silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions give a white solid, silver chloride.

screens.title: Key words
defs: An insoluble solid formed when two solutions react.

screens.text: Signs of a reaction: black copper oxide and sulfuric acid make a blue solution. Which sign is this?
screens.why:
Copper oxide is a black solid.
After the reaction you see a blue solution, copper sulfate.
Black turned into blue.
So the sign is a colour change.
No bubbles and no solid formed, so it is not gas or precipitate.

screens.title: Match example and sign
screens.why:
Blue copper sulfate forming from black copper oxide: colour change.
Hydrogen bubbles from magnesium: gas given off.
Potassium in water gets hot: temperature change.
A white silver chloride solid from two solutions: precipitate.
screens.text: Match each book example to the sign of reaction it shows.
Signs of a reaction: which are signs of a chemical reaction? Tap all.
screens.why:
The book lists four signs.
They are colour change, gas given off, temperature change and a precipitate (a solid forms).
A moving container is not a change in the substances.
So it is not a sign.

screens.title: Sign of a reaction, or not?
screens.text: Sort each observation. Does it show a new substance forming?
items: A new gas, carbon dioxide, is made.
The bubbles are steam. It is still water.
Two clear solutions give a white solid
The sugar is still there. The tea tastes sweet.
A colour change: new substances formed.
screens.why:
Ask: is a new substance formed?
Fizzing, a new solid, or a new colour show a reaction.
Boiling water bubbles too, but the steam is still water.
Dissolved sugar is still sugar.
So boiling and dissolving are not signs.
screens.clue: Bubbles can come from boiling too. Was anything new made?

screens.text: Spot the sign: Hiwot leaves an iron nail outside. It turns reddish-brown. Which sign shows a reaction?
screens.why:
Iron is grey. Rust is reddish-brown.
Hiwot saw the colour change.
The new colour shows a new substance, rust, formed.
No bubbles and no solid from two solutions, so not gas or precipitate.
So the sign is a colour change.

test.text: Which word names a solid formed when two solutions mix?
test.why:
Some reactions of two solutions make an insoluble solid.
That solid is called a precipitate.
A reactant is a starting material, not the solid formed.
So the answer is precipitate.

test.text: Gas test: magnesium in hydrochloric acid gives off which gas?
test.why:
Magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen.
The gas in the bubbles is hydrogen.
Chlorine stays in magnesium chloride.
So the gas given off is hydrogen.

test.text: True or false: a temperature change can be a sign of a chemical reaction.
test.why:
In some reactions heat is given out. In others heat is taken in.
Potassium in water gets so hot the hydrogen burns.
So a temperature change is a sign: True.

test.text: Precipitates: silver nitrate + sodium chloride gives a white solid. Which substance is it?
test.why:
Silver nitrate + sodium chloride → silver chloride + sodium nitrate.
Sodium nitrate stays dissolved.
Silver chloride is insoluble, so it is the white solid.
The precipitate is silver chloride.

test.text: Signs of a reaction: which shows a chemical reaction AND a gas given off?
test.why:
Ice melting and salt dissolving make no new substance.
They are physical changes.
Baking soda and vinegar fizz: a new gas forms.
So baking soda fizzing shows a reaction and a gas.
